scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me break it down step by step.

First, the situation: The person is 18 and has a 7-year-old brother. The brother is sensitive to sleep, meaning if he doesn't get enough, he gets cranky the next day. The mom left the 18-year-old in charge and allowed a friend to come over. The brother, who's usually put to bed on time, wakes up because the older siblings and their friend are being loud. The brother wants to stay up and watch the movie. The 18-year-old says no, but the friend says yes. The 18-year-old is worried that if they try to make the brother go to bed, he'll throw a fit, which would be embarrassing and exhausting. So, they let him stay up, and he ends up falling asleep on the couch. The next day, the brother is cranky, and the mom gets mad at the 18-year-old for not enforcing bedtime.

The question is: Is it morally acceptable for the 18-year-old not to force the brother to go to bed?

Let me consider the factors. The brother is 7, so he's still young and might not fully understand the consequences of staying up late. The 18-year-old knows that if they try to enforce bedtime, it could lead to a tantrum, which is both exhausting and embarrassing. They also mention that the brother can put himself to bed, so maybe he's capable of understanding the routine.

On the other hand, the 18-year-old is in a position of responsibility. They were left in charge by the mom, so they have a duty to ensure the brother's well-being, which includes getting enough sleep. The brother ended up being cranky the next day, which supports the idea that he needed more sleep.

But the 18-year-old argues that two hours of missed sleep isn't a big deal and that the brother should learn about consequences. They also mention that the brother can put himself to bed, implying he's old enough to understand the routine.

I'm thinking about the balance between responsibility and the immediate consequences of enforcing a rule. The 18-year-old didn't want to deal with the tantrum, which is understandable, but they also have a responsibility to set boundaries. However, the brother is only 7, so he might not fully grasp the consequences yet. The 18-year-old's reasoning that two hours isn't a big deal might be valid, but the mom's reaction suggests she expects more from the 18-year-old in terms of enforcing the rules.

I'm leaning towards the action being morally acceptable because the 18-year-old considered the immediate consequences of forcing the brother to bed and chose the lesser of two evils. However, the mom's perspective is that they should have enforced the bedtime regardless, which complicates things.

But ultimately, the 18-year-old's decision to let the brother stay up was made with the brother's immediate well-being in mind, avoiding a tantrum and the associated stress. While the brother was cranky the next day, it's a minor consequence compared to the potential stress of a tantrum. Therefore, the action might be considered morally acceptable.
